title: [WT-18a] Docs: worker role docs mode-aware for the landed worktree path (WT-04..WT-09)
description:
Split from WT-18 (task-1b2e6fe3ba1343c8ab02271510131155) at the governor's request. The human approved switching this project to worktree mode early (#general msg-717a48e0; human: "cant we use worktrees and lets few coders runs?", then "lets dop it"). The shape follows architect-0fcb7226 in #architects msg-ba081c4f.

Objective: in worktree mode the wrapper starts the worker CLI inside .worktrees/<taskId> on moe/task/<taskId>; WT-04..WT-09 are all DONE. But docs/roles/worker.md lines 12-13 still tell workers to work in the project root and never in a .worktrees/ checkout. That would pull a worktree seat out into the control checkout. Make the worker role docs mode-aware, covering only behaviour that is already on HEAD.

Files:
- docs/roles/worker.md, lines 12-13.
- docs/roles/worker.reference.md: the using-git-worktrees row, the attribution paragraph, and where checkpoints and completions land.
- packages/moe-daemon/src/generated/initFiles.ts, regenerated from a `git clone --shared` snapshot. WT-18's checkRefs[1] has the recipe, and the GLOBAL no-in-place-build rail applies.

Line 12 ("worktree mode gates every completion") belongs here only if the planner confirms that HEAD's worktree path already ignores the gate scope. HEAD already runs `run_frozen_gate worktree` on the merged tree. Anything WT-10 still changes belongs to WT-18c.

NOT in scope:
- the unlanded route and the LANDING-CONFLICT:/LANDING-RETRY: resume (WT-11 has not landed; this goes to WT-18c);
- CLAUDE.md, scripts/CLAUDE.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (WT-18);
- the .moe/roles copies, which are synced.

This row has no dependencies: no open row plans these files, and the behaviour it describes is on HEAD. It must land before this project's worktree switch.
definitionOfDone: worker.md's landing rule is mode-aware. Shared mode keeps today's text about landing from the project root. Worktree mode says the wrapper already started you in .worktrees/<taskId> on moe/task/<taskId> and lands from there. Human-directed .worktrees/ checkouts are not forbidden outright, per the 10-30 WT-S note on WT-18.
worker.reference.md is mode-aware only as far as HEAD's wrappers go, and presents no WT-10 or WT-11 behaviour as shipped.
`npm run lint` passes (40-line cap); worker.md contains no concrete task id and keeps its test sentinels.

packages/moe-daemon/src/generated/initFiles.ts equals the generator output from the snapshot and changes only the worker-doc entries; the targetedContextGuidance, qaCommitPolicy and initFiles vitest files pass there.

implementationPlan.description:
docs/roles/worker.reference.md: make it mode-aware, only as far as the landed wrappers (WT-04..WT-09) and daemon (WT-01/WT-02) go. Use the Edit tool only.

(a) Line 28, the using-git-worktrees row:
- Keep 'Only when a human explicitly asks for a worktree.'
- Then: the post-flight lands only the project root (shared mode) or your task worktree (worktree mode). Edits in any other `.worktrees/` checkout are invisible to it; merge them back by hand.
- Never name one `task-*`: those are the wrapper's task worktrees.

(b) 'Commits, checkpoints and rescue refs':
- End the intro sentence with a period, then add: where the work lands depends on `get_context.workspace.mode`, `shared` (the default) or `worktree`.
- Put a '**Shared mode:**' label before the table.
- Keep the 3 table rows and the ASSERTED/PLANNED/TOOL/MEASURED paragraph byte-identical.

(c) After that paragraph, add a '**Worktree mode**' block.

Lead paragraph:
- A WORKING claim while `settings.worktreeMode` is `'on'`: the wrapper starts your CLI in `.worktrees/<taskId>` on branch `moe/task/<taskId>`, cut from the target (the literal `consolidationBranch`, else `main`).
- `MOE_WORKTREE_PATH`, `MOE_TASK_BRANCH` and `MOE_LAND_TARGET` name the three. `MOE_PROJECT_PATH` still names the control checkout, so build no write path from it.
- Later sessions of the task reuse the worktree. Dirt a crashed session left there is committed to the task branch before your CLI starts (`MOE_CHECKPOINT_RECOVERED`).

A 3-row Exit | What lands | Where table:
1. REVIEW (or DONE): your worktree's dirty paths are committed to `moe/task/<taskId>`, then the branch's net change lands as ONE squash completion commit, `feat(task-<id>): <title>` (or `fix(…)`), on the target. Without a git remote it lands by a compare-and-swap ref update; with one, by a non-forced push to origin's target.
2. Any other exit: a `wip(task-<id>): …` checkpoint on `moe/task/<taskId>` only, pushed per `checkpointPush`. The target and the control checkout never move.
3. A completion that cannot reach the target (for example a conflict with it, or the target moving under every round): nothing lands on the target, your bytes stay on `moe/task/<taskId>`, and a failed round also parks a rescue ref at that branch's tip.

Attribution paragraph:
- There is no baseline and no tier: every dirty path in the worktree lands, untracked ones included (gitignored files never show), so keep scratch files out.
- DENY still holds: the paths listed above, with no exception for your task record (a worktree has no `.moe/`), plus `.claude/skills/**`.
- An edit written into the control checkout is never landed or reverted. Post-flight reports it once as `MOE_WORKTREE_STRAY_EDIT`, in a task comment naming the paths, and a human decides.
- If you pass `currentBranch` to `moe.complete_task`, it must be `moe/task/<taskId>`; otherwise the call fails with `BRANCH-POLICY-FAIL:`.

(d) Practical rules: prefix bullet 1 with 'In shared mode,'. Change no other bullet.

Source anchors at HEAD e4e122cd (sh name, ps1 twin): provision_worktree/Initialize-MoeWorktree, prepare_worktree_launch/Initialize-MoeWorktreeLaunch, worktree_preflight, denied_wt/Test-MoeDenyPathWorktree, land_worktree_checkpoint/Invoke-MoeWorktreeCheckpoint, land_worktree_completion/Invoke-MoeWorktreeCompletion, worktree_stray_check; docs/MCP_SERVER.md 'Worktree branch rule (WT-02)'. Code beats the design doc.

WT-18c adds the unlanded-route row and the LANDING-CONFLICT:/LANDING-RETRY: rule; don't pre-empt them, and use none of the step-1 banned words (phrase failures as 'cannot reach the target'). Keep sentinels: 'memory-name inventory', 'once per session', 'sessionHandoff', 'END_SESSION', 'fresh wrapper preflight', 'Resource blocks (`resourceId`) keep the seat parked', 'isolated-clone delivery', 'moe.record_commit', 'fresh remote fetch', 'sessionId'. Never write '`nextAction` → `claim_next_task`' or 'are wrapper-called — do not call them yourself'.

implementationPlan.description:
Regenerate the daemon's vendored copy of the two docs. Read mem:convention-role-doc-edits-regenerate-initfiles, mem:gotcha-moe-doc-generated-artifacts and mem:gotcha-daemon-linux-snapshot-gate first. The planner checked HEAD e4e122cd: its initFiles.ts was byte-identical to the generator output, so only the two worker entries should change.

1. Snapshot with history:
   `H=$(git rev-parse HEAD); S=$(mktemp -d); git clone -q --shared --no-checkout . "$S/repo"; git -C "$S/repo" checkout -q --detach "$H"`
   Copy ONLY the two edited docs into `$S/repo/docs/roles/`. Then, in `$S/repo/packages/moe-daemon`:
   `env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH="$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin" bash -c 'npm ci --no-audit --no-fund --loglevel=error && npm run generate-init-files'`
   Expect `Generated … (8 role docs + 3 subagents, sha-stamped)`.
2. `diff -u packages/moe-daemon/src/generated/initFiles.ts "$S/repo/packages/moe-daemon/src/generated/initFiles.ts"`. Expected hunks:
   - the 'worker.md' and 'worker.reference.md' ROLE_DOCS entries: the `<!-- moe-generated: sha=… -->` marker plus the edited or added lines. They sit inside a template literal, where `\` becomes `\\`, a backtick becomes `\`` and `${` becomes `\${`;
   - one new sha in each of those two SHIPPED_ROLE_BODY_SHAS lists, in sorted position.
3. Apply each hunk to the tree's initFiles.ts with the Edit tool.
   - NEVER cp, mv or redirect the generated file into the tree. A shell write leaves no TOOL witness, and WT-18 and WT-18c declare this path, so the landing would hold it (GLOBAL rail 3).
   - The Edit tool trims a trailing space in new_string: end every substring on a non-space character.
   - The memory's difflib pair recipe helps if there are many hunks.
4. `cmp` the tree's file with the clone's output; they must be equal.

If the diff shows a hunk for any other doc, HEAD went stale after e4e122cd. Apply that hunk too so cmp passes, and in the completion summary name the doc and the commit that changed it.

Error handling: if the clone, npm ci or the generator fails, rerun once. If it fails again, report_blocked with the error tail and blockedOnTaskIds []. Never run npm in the shared checkout's packages (GLOBAL rail 1).

(b) Safety negatives intact:
- the push is never forced;
- the target never moves on a failed landing;
- stray edits are never landed or reverted;

(c) Shared-mode text is unchanged apart from the mode labels. Line 12 is identical, worker.md has at most 40 lines, every sentinel is kept, and there is no task id.

(d) `git diff -U0 -- packages/moe-daemon/src/generated/initFiles.ts` touches only the two worker entries and their sha lists.

(e) Every changed path was written by the Edit tool and is listed in complete_step.modifiedFiles.

Fix anything found, rerun step 4's command fresh, and submit THAT output.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- Adding a worktree gate clause to line 12 ("worktree mode gates every completion"): rejected. HEAD's merged-tree gate, scope bypass and land lease come only from WT-10's WIP checkpoint d3441bf3, and WT-10 is still WORKING. The landed WT-08 path refuses gated worktree completions instead. This goes to WT-18c (comment-9ccc2f59 on it).
- Interleaving mode qualifiers into every shared-mode sentence of the reference: rejected. A separate Worktree mode block with its own table keeps the shared text byte-identical, and gives WT-18c an obvious slot for its unlanded row.
- Copying the generated initFiles.ts back with cp: rejected. A shell write leaves no TOOL witness, and WT-18/WT-18c declare the path, so it would be held. Hunks are applied with Edit, then cmp.
- `npm run build` in the clone (WT-18's recipe): `npm run generate-init-files` gives byte-identical output and is faster. vitest imports the file, so a syntax slip still fails.
- git clone --shared of '.' without a detached checkout: replaced by an explicit HEAD sha, so the snapshot is exactly this checkout's HEAD in either mode.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- Role docs reach agents through the plugin bundle and through the daemon's ROLE_DOCS. ROLE_DOCS holds initFiles.ts template literals (`\`, backtick and `${` escaped) and upgrades .moe/roles by marker sha.
- Daemon tests pin sentinel phrases in both the source and the generated copies (targetedContextGuidance, qaCommitPolicy, blockedSeatGuidance). daemonGitDocs bans "never runs/touches git"-style phrases in docs/roles/worker.md.
- Worktree mode is pinned per attempt: only a WORKING claim with settings.worktreeMode 'on' gets get_context.workspace.mode 'worktree'.
- The landed worktree path in moe-agent.sh is provision_worktree → prepare_worktree_launch → worktree_preflight → land_worktree_checkpoint / land_worktree_completion → worktree_stray_check. Its ps1 twins are named in the step-2 anchors.
planningNotes.risks:
- Presenting WT-10/WT-11 behaviour as shipped. The verification bans their vocabulary and pins line 12.
- Shell writes leave no TOOL witness, and WT-18/WT-18c declare the same three files, so the landing would hold them (MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED_UNTOUCHED). Use the Edit tool for all three.
- The Edit tool trims trailing spaces in new_string, so cmp fails unless every substring ends on a non-space character.
- HEAD's initFiles.ts can go stale before execution if a peer lands a role-doc edit. The regen then carries a foreign hunk: include it so cmp passes, and report it.
- daemonGitDocs regex: avoid 'never touches git', 'runs no git' and 'does not run git' wording.
- 'unlanded' is WT-11 vocabulary: phrase failures as 'cannot reach the target'.
- Never run npm ci/build/test in the shared checkout's packages. The env -i clone with nvm node v24.21.0 is the only place.
